title: POC Cutover Readiness and Traffic Shift Playbook
next_steps: Redwood to send final canary runbook and rollback checklist (Connor) by 2025-08-16
Nimbus to validate telemetry thresholds and share dashboard access (Priya) by 2025-08-18
Schedule dry-run cutover in staging with live traffic replay (all) target 2025-08-20
Redwood to provide post-cutover escalation contact list and on-call rotation (Maya) by 2025-08-15
action_items: Connor: upload canary runbook to shared Confluence and link to runbook doc (due 2025-08-16)
Priya: export current SLO/SLA baseline metrics and share Grafana links (due 2025-08-18)
Liam: confirm network egress firewall rules for Redwood Private node IPs (due 2025-08-15)
Ethan: review KMS key access and provide list of approved IAM roles (due 2025-08-17)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on go-live cutover planning. Reviewed canary strategy (5% -> 25% -> 100%), smoke tests, monitoring thresholds, rollback criteria, and security signoffs. Identified five concrete action items: runbook, telemetry access, firewall confirmation, KMS/IAM list, and a staging dry-run. Agreement to schedule a staged traffic shift and for Redwood to provide escalation contacts and a succinct rollback checklist.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: OK, welcome everyone. Thanks for making time. We're aiming to get through cutover readiness and a concrete traffic shift playbook today. I see Nimbus folks, hi.
[00:08] Dana Ruiz: Hey, thanks. We want this to be a practical checklist — not theory. We have execs looking for a firm cutover date after the dry-run.
[00:15] Connor Liu: Quick agenda, we'll cover the proposed canary percentages and timing, smoke tests, monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds, network/security checks, and then assign action items.
[00:27] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. FYI we've got a couple of constraints: our ingress LB supports weighted routing, but we have a third-party edge that can introduce sticky sessions. Need to consider session affinity behavior.
[00:36] Priya Sharma: Also want to make sure our error budget calc is consistent — current SLO is 99.5 p95 latency under 600ms and error rate under 0.5% for user-facing requests.
[00:46] Maya Patel: Great. Connor, can you run through the canary proposal?
[00:50] Connor Liu: Sure. Proposed traffic shift: Step 0: baseline tests in staging with traffic replay. Step 1: 5% of production traffic to Redwood inference variant for 2 hours (smoke + perf). Step 2: if green, 25% for 6 hours with full telemetry, run longer tail tests. Step 3: 100% cutover after 24-hour validation and stakeholder signoff. We also recommend a blue/green fallback so we can switch back to current model instantly.
[01:20] Zoe Miller: Who's owning the green/blue switch? Our platform needs an automated route.
[01:24] Liam O'Connor: We can script weighted changes in the LB; but we need an API that updates weights quickly. Connor, does Redwood expose a low-latency route-change API?
[01:34] Connor Liu: We have a routing control API and a manual console toggle. Low-latency changes should be under 5s for published config — caveat network propagation times. We'll provide the API keys for staging and a small playbook on how to call it.
[01:45] Priya Sharma: On monitoring, what metrics should we be watching aside from latency and error rate?
[01:50] Grace Hernandez: Recommended set: p50/p95/p99 latency, request error rate, 95th token generation time, token-per-request cost estimate, KV cache hit ratio, GPU utilization, queue depth, and end-to-end tail latency for API gateway. Also, SLO burn rate alerts and a synthetic health check hitting the exact prompt patterns of your top 10 flows.
[02:13] Ethan Park: Regarding security, KMS access review is needed. Our policy requires separate keys per environment and an allow-list of Redwood service principal. Also audit logs need to be forwarded to our SIEM.
[02:25] Maya Patel: Understood. We'll include KMS roles and the audit export config in the security appendix of the runbook. Connor, quick note: include the SIEM forwarding instructions.
[02:33] Connor Liu: Will do. Also, for rollback criteria, propose: any sustained p95 breach over 2x SLO for 30 minutes OR error rate >1% for 15 minutes triggers automatic rollback to previous weight. Manual override allowed for on-call.
[02:50] Dana Ruiz: Can we get the exact alert thresholds in writing? Execs want crisp pass/fail criteria.
[02:55] Maya Patel: Yes — we'll add an appendix table in the runbook with exact thresholds (e.g., p95 > 1200ms for 30m => rollback).
[03:05] Liam O'Connor: About session affinity: if sticky sessions are enabled, the first hit must route consistently to the same variant. We might need to flush session cookies or add a hashing key.
[03:14] Connor Liu: We suggest short TTL cookies for the canary window, plus a client-side header to control affinity for test users. We'll document the header approach in staging runs.
[03:24] Priya Sharma: For the dry-run, timeline? We'd prefer next week.
[03:28] Maya Patel: Proposed dry-run: 2025-08-20 in staging with live traffic replay and 1-hour smoke then 3-hour performance window. Nimbus team to supply a traffic replay dump.
[03:38] Zoe Miller: We can provide a sanitized traffic dump, yes. Also want a rehearsal with the runbook owners beforehand.
[03:44] Grace Hernandez: We'll schedule a 30-minute rehearsal run on 2025-08-19 for runbook walkthrough and role assignments.
[03:50] Ethan Park: On the audit logs, how long does Redwood retain logs in hosted vs private? We have retention rules for 12 months.
[03:58] Maya Patel: For Private deployments customers control retention; for hosted we keep 90 days by default but enterprise retention add-on available. We'll include retention options in the security appendix.
[04:08] Liam O'Connor: Network cutover: need confirmation of egress IPs so our firewall team can allow traffic. Connor?
[04:13] Connor Liu: We'll provide the CIDR blocks for the private node pool and dedicated endpoints; in private deployments the nodes are inside your VPC so fewer egress concerns, but for Dedicated/Hosted we provide fixed IP ranges — I'll attach the list.
[04:25] Priya Sharma: Any recommended smoke test prompts? Our top 10 flows include patient lookup and appointment booking; they involve structured json outputs.
[04:34] Connor Liu: We'll provide prompt recipes for each flow, and a structured output validator that checks if the JSON schema matches. Add assertion tests for required fields and value ranges.
[04:45] Dana Ruiz: On risk, what about model quality regressions? We want to ensure responses aren't hallucinating critical fields.
[04:52] Grace Hernandez: Our quality monitoring includes prompt set evals and automatic regression alerts based on BLEU-like and schema pass rates. During canary, run the eval set and block promotion if regression exceeds configured thresholds.
[05:04] Zoe Miller: Ok, can the eval be run automatically as part of the 25% window?
[05:08] Connor Liu: Yes, we can schedule eval runs and store artifacts in your S3 for review. We'll add that to the runbook schedule.
[05:16] Liam O'Connor: Regarding A/B testing vs canary: are we recommending A/B for user experience experiments or pure canary for safety?
[05:24] Maya Patel: For this go-live we recommend pure canary for safety. A/B can be done later for feature experiments. Canary gives you quick rollback and performance proof.
[05:33] Ethan Park: How long is the recommended watch period at 100% before we consider it stable?
[05:37] Connor Liu: We usually recommend 24-72 hours of steady-state monitoring, with key stakeholder signoff after 24h if all metrics stable. For Nimbus, because of regulatory needs, consider 72 hours with audit review.
[05:50] Priya Sharma: Let's plan for 48 hours as a compromise, with a hard re-eval at 24h and final signoff at 48h.
[05:59] Dana Ruiz: Sounds reasonable. Who signs off — is it VP Product plus SRE lead?
[06:03] Zoe Miller: We require product + SRE + security signoff for production cutover.
[06:09] Maya Patel: We'll add a signoff template. Connor: include explicit owner fields and contact numbers for escalation.
[06:15] Connor Liu: Yep. Also including on-call rotation: Redwood will provide a 24/7 escalation roster for the first 72 hours post-cutover.
[06:24] Liam O'Connor: Fine. Now, small note — cost monitoring. During canary we want token-cost-per-request estimates to ensure no surprises.
[06:32] Grace Hernandez: We'll enable token breakdown in the telemetry so you can see cost estimation per route and per model. Also suggest a soft cap alert if cost projection exceeds 20% of expected.
[06:43] Priya Sharma: For observability access, can we get read-only Grafana links and API keys?
[06:47] Connor Liu: Yes, will provide read-only dashboard links. We'll also export a set of sample queries to your Prometheus/Grafana.
[06:56] Ethan Park: On the rollback path, manual vs automatic, what are the human-in-the-loop expectations?
[07:01] Maya Patel: Automatic rollback will trigger for defined threshold violations; manual rollback can be initiated by product or SRE leads. We'll document the approval flow: SRE can trigger immediately; product lead to be notified.
[07:10] Zoe Miller: Good. Can we get a short checklist of pre-cutover gates? Example: backup config, DB migrations validated, canary keys created, plan B endpoints ready.
[07:19] Connor Liu: We'll include a pre-cutover gate checklist: (1) backups & snapshots taken, (2) config freeze initiated, (3) network rules validated, (4) telemetry alerts created, (5) rollback plan staged and tested in staging.
[07:31] Dana Ruiz: What about change windows and stakeholder comms? Execs want a 30-minute heads-up before each weight increase.
[07:37] Maya Patel: We'll make that part of the runbook communications plan — and include Slack channel mentions, PagerDuty escalations, and a post-shift status message template.
[07:46] Liam O'Connor: A small technical question: KV cache priming — should we pre-warm the cache before canary?
[07:52] Connor Liu: Yes, for certain flows we recommend priming KV cache with last-known context for the most frequent prompts; include a script to run a batch of warmup calls before the 25% window.
[08:02] Priya Sharma: Are there any limitations on batch sizes or concurrency to avoid hitting GPU memory limits?
[08:08] Connor Liu: We'll set guardrails in the runbook: max concurrency per node and batch sizes tuned to your model variant. For your workload we recommend max concurrency 32 and batch size 16 for the first run, we can tune after observed metrics.
[08:21] Ethan Park: For compliance, will audit logs show prompt contents, or are they redacted? We need PII controls.
[08:28] Maya Patel: By default we redact PII in hosted logs, but for Private deployments you control raw logs. We can add a tokenization/pass-through option and a redaction pipeline; we'll include options and recommended config in the security appendix.
[08:40] Zoe Miller: I'd like to see sample audit log entries. Can Redwood provide a sanitized example?
[08:44] Connor Liu: Yes, we'll attach sanitized log samples to the runbook.
[08:47] Grace Hernandez: Quick timing recap: dry-run in staging 2025-08-20, rehearsal on 2025-08-19, runbook to be delivered 2025-08-16, telemetry links by 2025-08-18.
[08:57] Dana Ruiz: Sounds good. One more: what about A/B revenue experiments — do we block that during the initial two weeks?
[09:02] Maya Patel: Recommended no A/B experiments during the 48-72 hour stabilization window. After stabilization, A/B experiments can be scheduled with non-zero traffic splits.
[09:12] Liam O'Connor: Any hard dependencies from our side we missed?
[09:15] Priya Sharma: We need the KMS role list and firewall CIDRs.
[09:18] Ethan Park: Also a legal checklist for data residency and contractual SLAs for the Dedicated offering.
[09:22] Maya Patel: We'll push the legal checklist and a summary SLA matrix. Connor will include the Dedicated option differences.
[09:30] Connor Liu: I'll post the runbook draft after the call. It will include step-by-step commands, playbook links, Slack templates, alert thresholds, and a rollback checklist.
[09:38] Zoe Miller: Can you add a small section on user-facing degraded behavior messaging? We want canned UX copy for when we intentionally enable a degraded mode.
[09:44] Grace Hernandez: We'll add status page copy and templated error messaging that maps to specific rollback criteria.
[09:51] Dana Ruiz: Great. Any blockers preventing us from the dry-run?
[09:55] Liam O'Connor: Pending firewall and KMS confirmations.
[09:58] Priya Sharma: Also need the traffic dump.
[10:00] Maya Patel: OK solid. Let's go around quickly for final confirmations. Connor?
[10:04] Connor Liu: I confirm runbook delivery 8/16; run rehearsal 8/19; staging dry-run 8/20. I'll attach runbook link and IP list.
[10:11] Liam O'Connor: Nimbus will get KMS list and firewall rule names by 8/15 and traffic dump by 8/17.
[10:18] Priya Sharma: We'll share Grafana read-only links by 8/18.
[10:22] Ethan Park: I'll review the audit log redaction options and sign off.
[10:26] Maya Patel: Awesome, thank you. We'll follow up with concise runbook and the escalation roster. Meeting adjourned.
[10:32] -- End of recording --

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hear of product names (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cache"), some punctuation and speaker attribution may be imperfect. Artifacts referenced: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/nimbus-cutover (runbook placeholder), https://grafana.nimbus.example/d/overview (read-only dash - to be shared).
